A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same finite-sample analysis of prediction-powered inference. Their main texts, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original AlphaFold and Galaxies experiments measuring estimation error, confidence-interval coverage, and interval width.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C–D retain the work's original AlphaFold and Galaxies experimental results.

M1.justification: The single-sample and two-fold cross-fit estimators retain their covariance-based tuning and estimation procedures. V1's separately defined split-sample estimator becomes the fold-level estimate in v2. Redefining n as total labels does not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: AlphaFold and Galaxies remain the empirical datasets, with the same binary-label mean-estimation tasks and pseudo-label noise scenarios. The new analytical heatmap explores the existing binary setting; the M-estimation discussion introduces no evaluated task.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 1 adds original PPI as an explicitly evaluated comparator alongside Classical and Cross-fit PPI++ in an analytical variance comparison. The comparator sets in the retained real-data experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: The new analytical comparison fixes P(F=1)=0.20 and compares n=20 versus n=50 while varying positive and negative predictive values. Existing experimental sampling, noise construction, metrics, and budgets remain unchanged; the revised n versus 2n notation does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: V2 Figure 1 adds an analytical sensitivity example showing how estimator preference changes with pseudo-label quality and label availability. Existing noise and sample-size analyses are retained. Appendix D relocates v1 Figure 2b rather than adding a robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50,000 bootstrap draws, random-state resetting, and the same confidence-interval coverage evaluation. V2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, uncertainty displays, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: V2 Figure 1 adds analytical winner regions: the illustrated belief region has no uniformly preferred estimator at n=20, whereas Cross-fit PPI++ dominates there at n=50. All earlier empirical plot contents are retained. The newly stated 87% coverage at n=20 was already visible in v1 Figure 2a.

T1.justification: V2 adds the finite-N Gaussian improvement condition and its derivation in Proposition 4.2 and Appendix A.9.3, and explicitly proves Gaussian cross-fold covariance cancellation. It removes v1's signed-binary Proposition 4.4 and Appendix A.4.3 proof. The central infinite-N variance decomposition and covariance-error result are retained through consolidation and equivalent sample-size notation.

C1.justification: The central no-free-lunch, correlation-threshold, bias, and undercoverage claims remain. V2 explicitly broadens the practical contribution to choosing among Classical, PPI, and PPI++ using assumed pseudo-label quality, and drops the abstract's explicit statement of an analogous binary-label bound.

C2.justification: Remark 3.1 newly explains relevance to M-estimation through gradient means while distinguishing this from a finite-sample parameter guarantee. The introduction and Discussion also clarify that estimator selection requires prior quality assumptions and explain why the required correlation can be reasonable at moderate sample sizes.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain the same binary-noise construction, treatment of remaining observations as unlabeled, random-state resetting, and ddof=1 instructions. No implementation resources, hardware information, or code/data access instructions are added.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning through control-variate and survey-sampling literature, including Lavenberg and Welch, Nelson, Cassel and colleagues, and Mozer. It acknowledges that the infinite-N single-sample Gaussian threshold corresponds to an existing result and distinguishes its distribution-free contribution. The Impact Statement adds substantial application-related literature.

P1.justification: V2 reorganizes the theoretical narrative around a direct cross-fit variance theorem, absorbs the standalone split-sample treatment, and substantially restructures Appendix A. It expands related work, replaces the short conclusion with a developed Discussion, adds an Impact Statement, and rewrites explanatory passages throughout.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, adds the decision-map figure, and substantially rearranges figure placement and panel organization. V1's AlphaFold coverage figure is split between v2 Figures 3 and 6, and the AlphaFold MSE panels become vertically stacked. Retained empirical plots display the same results.

improvement.justification: V2 improves usability through the direct variance decomposition, explicit total-label notation, and decision-map example with stated assumptions. Its expanded historical positioning more accurately distinguishes inherited Gaussian insights from the general contribution, and the finite-N analysis broadens applicability. Although the explicit signed-binary specialization is removed, the central theory and empirical evidence remain available. These changes support a limited net improvement in clarity, attribution, and practical guidance.
